newsitem.title: UK: BA expects swift progress on open skies.
newsitem.headline: BA expects swift progress on open skies.

text.p: British Airways chief executive Robert Ayling said on Tuesday that he expected significant progress in the stalled "open skies" aviation talks between the U.S. and Britain this month.
"I expect significant progress on an open skies agreement by the end of September," he told reporters at a news briefing.

The remarks follow demands by rivals to British Airway's controversial plans to link with American Airlines. The rivals say BA must give up some of its 38 percent share of slots at London's Heathrow airport to prevent the combination donminating the market.
The U.S. government has made access to slots at Heathrow a key issue in its "open skies" talks with Britian, which broke doqwn last week.
Previous efforts at getting an agreement to liberalise the transatlantic market have foundered on the Heathrow issue.

Despite the contentious issue of the Heathrow slots, Ayling does not believe BA will necessarily be forced to relinquish some of its prized landing slots at Heathrow, Europe's busines airport. "I do not accept that we will have to give up some of the 38 percent share," he said.
